problems.source_says: The paper never says that ChatGPT was unavailable in the phase a Study 3 participant was not assigned to. The system only guided GenAI use during specific phases. Appendix G sets two 10-minute phases with no AI rule, and Appendix H covers only the intelligence manipulation. Under the form's own Study 2b convention, the elaboration arm is yes either way. The generation arm is mixed only if AI was barred while elaborating. So 'mixed' rests on an assumption, which the form itself lists as unresolved. The question code (with_ai) does not change.
problems.quote: we developed a custom online system that guided participants’ interactions with GenAI during specific creative phases (Chen & Chan, 2024).

problems.source_says: Every confidence interval in the paper belongs to an indirect (mediated) effect through a self-reported mediator, or to a moderated-mediation index. None belongs to the AI contrast on rated novelty or usefulness. Listing confidence_interval for these contrasts invites the codebook's CI-to-SE conversion (section 10) for the wrong estimand. The 'reported' text and the notes say this, but the structured field does not. The field should list only arm_means_sds_ns (Studies 2a and 2b) or standardized_effect (Study 3).
problems.quote: the indirect effect of human–GenAI collaboration in the idea generation phase on novelty through cognitive flexibility was significant (estimate = 0.17, 95 % CI = [0.033, 0.341])
problems.locator: p. 6, Sections 5.1.3 and 5.2.3; p. 8, Section 6.3.3; p. 9 (Hypothesis 7)

problems.form_value: treatment = GenAI in idea generation phase; control = GenAI in idea elaboration phase; direction = treatment_lower
problems.source_says: For usefulness, the paper proposes and tests collaboration in the elaboration phase against the generation phase (H5, coded 1 = idea elaboration). The codebook makes the tested configuration the treatment arm of an ai_design contrast. That gives treatment = elaboration arm and direction = treatment_higher (r = 0.42 with CP coded 1 = elaboration). The form uses the generation arm as treatment for both Study 3 outcomes. Low severity: both arms are named and the printed r is correct, but the sign under codebook section 7 flips.
problems.quote: human–GenAI collaboration in the idea elaboration phase (compared with the generation phase) improves creative usefulness by reducing cognitive overload.
problems.locator: p. 1, Abstract; pp. 3-4, Section 2.2.2 (H5); p. 8, Section 6.3.3 (Hypothesis 5)

confirmed: Criterion 3: three marketing experts, blind to purpose, hypotheses, and conditions, rated each participant's creative proposal for novelty and usefulness. Study 3 used the same approach (ICC2 0.82 and 0.84). No outcome in the form is self-reported. (p. 5, Section 5.1.2; p. 7, Section 6.2)
Cognitive flexibility and cognitive overload are self-report scales, and the form correctly leaves them out of the outcomes. (p. 5, Section 5.1.2; p. 6, Section 5.2.2; p. 14, Appendix I)

Constructs: novelty is 'the degree of innovation and uniqueness of the proposal and advertising copy', and usefulness is practical implementation and solving real problems. Both are rated on single outputs. The paper has no diversity or idea-count measure. (pp. 5-6, Section 5.1.2)
Unit = participant: 'the average score from the three experts was taken as the final score for each participant'. Tables 1-3 have N = 42, 44, and 198 people. (p. 6; Tables 1-3, pp. 6-8)

AI availability S2 = mixed and S3 = yes: Appendix E allows GenAI in the generation phase and bars it in the elaboration phase, and Appendix F reverses this. Both codes assume the experts rated the final 'creative proposal of at least 100 words' (Appendix D). The paper implies this but does not state it. (p. 13, Appendices D-F)

Question = with_ai for all six outcomes: none is a diversity outcome. The Study 2a proposal elaborates the AI-assisted preliminary ideas within one 20-minute task, so it is not unassisted work after AI use (after_ai). (p. 13, Appendices D-E)

Table 1 matches: Novelty H 5.44 (0.55), GenAI 6.05 (0.59), r = 0.14; USEN H 5.21 (0.45), GenAI 5.37 (0.52), r = −0.06; ICC2 novelty 0.82/0.85, usefulness 0.87/0.82; indirect effect 0.17, 95% CI [0.033, 0.341]. (p. 6, Table 1; Sections 5.1.2-5.1.3)

Table 2 matches: USEN H 5.49 (0.39), GenAI 5.89 (0.39), r = 0.30; Novelty H 5.31 (0.47), GenAI 5.43 (0.49), r = 0.39**; ICC2 novelty 0.79/0.74, usefulness 0.91/0.93; indirect effect 0.14, 95% CI [0.056, 0.222]. (p. 7, Table 2; p. 6, Sections 5.2.2-5.2.3)

Study 3 directions: Section 6.3.1 codes CP 1 = idea elaboration for Table 3. Under that coding, the CF and CO correlations (−0.30, −0.35) agree with the printed t-tests (4.41, 5.22). So the generation arm scores higher on novelty and lower on usefulness, as the form records. (p. 8, Sections 6.3.1 and 6.3.3)
Study 2 directions: the GenAI condition mean is higher on all four outcomes. No study prints a test of the total AI effect on novelty or usefulness. (pp. 6-8, Tables 1-3; Sections 5.1.3, 5.2.3, 6.3)

No missing outcome: each study scores only novelty and usefulness on output. No composite creativity score is reported, and no contrast by the perceived-intelligence factor on novelty or usefulness is printed (Fig. 2 concerns self-reported overload). (pp. 5-9)
Primary codes follow the hypotheses: H1a (novelty) for Study 2a, H1b (usefulness) for Study 2b, H3 and H5 for Study 3. The AsPredicted preregistration is not in the PDF. (pp. 3-4; p. 7, Section 6.1)
summary: All six outcomes are expert ratings of the participants' written proposals, and their constructs, participant unit, with_ai question codes, and every reported number match Tables 1-3 and Sections 5-6 of the PDF, so criterion 3 holds through Study 3 (198 people). The coding is refuted on three details: Study 3's 'mixed' AI availability assumes a phase restriction the paper never states, the 'confidence_interval' entries belong to indirect effects rather than to the AI contrasts, and the Study 3 usefulness contrast names the generation arm as treatment although the paper tests the elaboration arm.
